content: The American Diabetes Association recommends engaging in moderate-intensity physical activity, such as brisk walking, for a minimum of 150 minutes per week. This level of activity is particularly beneficial for individuals at risk of developing type 2 diabetes as well as those diagnosed with prediabetes. Regular moderate-intensity exercise improves the body’s sensitivity to insulin and helps reduce the accumulation of abdominal fat in both children and adults. Additionally, interrupting prolonged periods of sedentary behavior and incorporating resistance training exercises can further decrease the likelihood of developing diabetes. Physical activity has also been demonstrated to play a significant role in reducing the risk of gestational diabetes in pregnant women.
